notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-442dc5 (issue #1382). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files.

Provenance. Both arXiv hashes match byte for byte: the v2 PDF b48dad0a...5853c4 and the v2 e-print 287a8f27...ddc1b6a (a single arXiv22Aug2023.tex of 3469 lines, exactly as recorded). The two Cambridge hashes cannot be reproduced - the publisher stamps each download, which this extraction does not say, though its sibling extraction of Ichino-Prasanna does - and I verified the Corrigendum claim directly: Forum of Mathematics Pi 12 (2024) e5 corrects only the affiliation 'Universität Duisberg Essen' to 'Universität Duisburg-Essen', so none of the nine findings is addressed by it.

Numbering and coverage. The class hangs conj, lem, cor, thm, defi, examp, warning, remar, remark and nota on the prop counter with \newtheorem{prop}{Proposition}[section], so numbers are section.n and the appendix is lettered A. Simulating that gives 138 numbered statements and reproduces the number and the kind of every statement the findings cite: Lemma 3.1, Lemma 3.30, Corollary 3.38, Proposition 3.48, Lemma 3.57, Lemma 4.30, Lemma 6.5 and Lemma A.7.

Coverage was 137 of 138. The single uncovered statement was Remark 1.7, and it is not commentary: it is the transfer of every section 1 theorem from framed to versal and universal deformation rings, with its two named inputs (Iyengar Lemma 2.1 for formal smoothness, Bruns-Herzog Theorem 2.3.6 and Corollary 2.2.23(a)). I have added it as item 148, routed to the local Part II beside the theorems it extends.

Mistakes in the paper. All nine are confirmed, each quoted verbatim from the source. Seven are notational and each is settled by the surrounding text: the upper limit n for d in a characteristic-polynomial identity whose coefficients are indexed 0..d (E1); X^ps_j := R^ps_j without Spec (E2); GL_d(k) where the pseudo-character has dimension d_i and the next display writes GL_{d_i} (E3); U_max inside Xbar^ps where the proof works in X^ps (E4); a scheme-theoretic image taken in the wrong direction, X^ps inside X^ps_Sigma, where iota_Sigma goes the other way (E5); and 'the universal deformation ring of R_{rho_x}' for rho_x (E6).

E7 is a genuine error in a proof: psi is defined by psi(x) = sigma(x varpi_F^{-v(x)})^a, so psi(varpi_F) = 1 and psi kappa^{-1}(varpi_F) = kappa(varpi_F)^{-1}, which need not be congruent to 1 modulo varpi; the entry's unramified twist repairs it and the lemma stands. E9 is an error affecting nothing: Lemma 3.30's final inequality, and the corresponding final steps of Lemmas A.7 and A.8, are false for d = 1, which the paper nowhere excludes, though every application has d >= 2.

E8, extended. E8 records four citations whose word disagrees with the kind of the statement cited. I audited that class exhaustively - all 329 word-plus-\ref citations in the source against the environment carrying each label - and found exactly five mismatches: the four recorded, plus 'see the proof of Proposition 4.18' in the proof of Theorem 5.6, where 4.18 is Corollary 4.18. I have added that instance to E8 rather than opening a near-duplicate entry. All five survive into the published text, which I checked page by page; in that PDF's text layer the citation words and numbers are interleaved with mathematics, so a naive search under-reports them - my first pass wrongly suggested three had been fixed in production.

Routes. Five source routes and two Part IIs, all accepted; see the route verdicts. Both Part II titles reproduce their parents' verbatim, and the local Part II is where the paper's own content sits: the parent plans local deformation rings and their potentially semistable quotients, not the complete-intersection property, the components of the special fibre, normality, or the density theorem. There are no library items, which is right for this subject; the 11 planned items cite layers that all exist in data/atlas.json.

Verdict: accept.
